lessonRef.subject: financial-literacy
lessonRef.unitTitle: PF4 — Using Credit: Debt Strategy and Repayment Analysis
lessonRef.title: Unit performance task: student loan repayment plan structures in outline

focus: student loan repayment plan structures in outline
objective: Build a complete fictional repayment plan across three debts, quantify what the current position costs each year, and defend an ordering against a stated objective.
scenario: Perpetua Olufemi-Strand holds the three fictional debts below and is building a repayment plan. All balances, rates, payments, and income figures are invented for this performance task.
safetyNotes: Every figure, person, employer, institution, offer, account, and document on this task sheet is fictional and exists only for practice.
No real transaction is part of this lesson, and no real bank, card, brokerage, tax, or login detail is ever requested. If a task sheet ever appears to ask for one, stop and tell a trusted adult.
This lesson teaches general financial concepts and does not advise anyone about their own money. For a real decision, talk with a trusted adult or a qualified licensed professional.
materials: the fictional debt and income figures in these directions

tasks.directions: The study loan holds $19,400 at 5.9% a year with a $214 minimum. The card holds $3,150 at 23.4% a year with a $95 minimum. The vehicle loan holds $8,700 at 6.4% a year with a $265 minimum. Monthly interest is the annual rate divided by 12. Perpetua takes home $3,960 a month and can put $820 a month towards debt. Her gross income is $5,100 a month.

prompts.text: How much interest does the study loan charge in the first month?
How much interest does the card charge in the first month?
How much interest does the vehicle loan charge in the first month?
What is the total interest charged across all three debts in the first month?

tasks.directions: Now build the plan from her capacity.

prompts.text: What do the three minimum payments come to?
How much does she have above the minimums, from her $820 debt capacity?
If nothing changed, what would the first month’s interest come to over a year?
Directing the extra $246.00 at the card, how many months does it take to clear? Ignore interest for this step and give one decimal place.
What is Perpetua’s debt-to-income ratio, using the minimums against her $5,100 gross income? Give one decimal place.
What share of her $3,960 take-home pay does the $820 debt capacity represent? Give one decimal place.
Directing the $246.00 at the card rather than the study loan moves it from 5.9% to 23.4%. How much interest does that save in a month?
Which debt should receive the extra $246.00 first if the objective is to minimise interest paid?

Present a repayment plan for Perpetua. State the ordering and the objective it serves, say what happens to the freed-up payment when the card clears, and name the assumption whose failure would most damage the plan.
Perpetua’s debt-to-income ratio is 11.3% and her debt capacity is 20.7% of take-home pay. Explain why the two figures differ so much, and say which one describes her situation better.

remediation: If the extra available comes out at $820, the minimum payments are not being deducted. The $574.00 of minimums has to be paid on all three debts before anything can be directed, so only $246.00 is actually a choice. Write the capacity as one row, the minimums as three rows, and the remainder as the directable figure before choosing any ordering.
extension: Work out what Perpetua could direct each month once both the card and the vehicle loan are cleared, and say what that does to the time the study loan takes.
